statement: The Cholesky decomposition or Cholesky factorization of a Hermitian, positive-definite matrix A is a decomposition into the product of a lower triangular matrix L and its conjugate transpose L*, such that A = L L* (or A = L L^T for real symmetric matrices). The supplied source defines this decomposition directly and provides algorithmic variants, update formulas, and existence proofs, but genuinely contains no derivation of the Cholesky factorization itself.

symbols.meaning: Hermitian, positive-definite matrix (or real symmetric positive-definite matrix)
conjugate transpose of lower triangular matrix L

diagonal matrix (or block diagonal matrix in block LDL^T decomposition)
updated matrix after rank modification or row/column insertion/removal
symbols.dimensions: n x n or m x m

properties.property: When applicable, the Cholesky decomposition is roughly twice as efficient as the LU decomposition for solving systems of linear equations.
properties.why: it exploits Hermitian symmetry and positive-definiteness to factor A directly into triangular factors

properties.property: For a symmetric matrix represented in block form, the block LDL^T decomposition yields recursive relations for diagonal blocks D_j = A_jj - sum_{k=1}^{j-1} L_jk D_k L_jk^T and off-diagonal blocks L_ij = (A_ij - sum_{k=1}^{j-1} L_ik D_k L_jk^T) D_j^{-1}.
properties.why: multiplying block L, D, and L^T matrices and equating block entries yields these recurrence relations

properties.property: The decomposition can be updated after a rank-one perturbation A_tilde = A + c x x* without recomputing the entire decomposition from scratch, provided A_tilde remains positive-definite.
properties.why: the existing factor L can be updated directly to yield the new factor L_tilde

properties.property: A rank-n update A_tilde = A + M M* can be computed via successive rank-one updates.
properties.why: successive rank-one updates are performed for each of the columns of M

properties.property: When rows and columns are inserted into or removed from A, the Cholesky factor of the resulting matrix can be found using triangular back/forward substitution and submatrix Cholesky updates.
properties.why: block relations equate submatrix products to triangular solves and Schur-type updates of the form A_tilde = A + c x x*

properties.property: Every positive semi-definite matrix admits a Cholesky factorization A = L L* with L lower triangular having non-negative diagonal entries.
properties.why: it follows by a limiting argument on A_k = A + (1/k) I_n or by applying QR decomposition to the matrix square root B* = Q R yielding A = R* R

assumptions.assumption: Matrix A is Hermitian (or real symmetric) and positive-definite (or positive semi-definite).
assumptions.breaks_when: A is non-Hermitian or indefinite with negative eigenvalues (or non-positive eigenvalues when strict positive-definiteness is required).

assumptions.assumption: In a rank-one update A_tilde = A + c x x*, the scalar c must preserve positive-definiteness.
assumptions.breaks_when: c is negative and large enough in magnitude to make A_tilde singular or indefinite.

failure_modes.mode: Factorization breakdown due to lack of positive-definiteness
failure_modes.signature: Algorithm encounters zero or negative pivots, or requires square roots/inversions of non-positive entries
failure_modes.cause: The input matrix A is indefinite, negative-definite, or singular when strict positive-definiteness is required

failure_modes.signature: Updated factor cannot be formed as a valid positive-definite Cholesky factor
failure_modes.cause: A negative scalar c causes the updated matrix A_tilde to lose positive-definiteness

failure_modes.mode: Block LDL^T inversion bottleneck or singularity
failure_modes.signature: Failure or numerical instability when computing D_j^{-1}
failure_modes.cause: A diagonal block D_j is singular, ill-conditioned, or too large for practical explicit inversion
